terra.problem: Saying the whole letter will keep circling divisions overstates what the letter covers.
The text does not say Paul names his sources so nobody can accuse him of spreading gossip.
The Christ line is last in the list, not in the middle.
The claim that Christ has the name above every other name needs a reference outside this passage.
“Only Christ was crucified” is too broad. Paul’s question is whether he was crucified for the Corinthians.
The explanation repeats the question’s answer without adding insight or Papa Dorin’s personality.
Paul adds Stephanas’s household in verse 16, not the next verse after verse 14.
Referring to the answer as “the one on the card” draws attention to the lesson interface.
The last two sentences are generic filler rather than an explanation in Papa Dorin’s voice.
Paul warns that the cross could be emptied of its power; he does not say fancy wording cannot add to it.
The cookie comparison trivializes the power of Christ’s cross instead of keeping the comparison on the human side.
Calling the message foolishness does not establish that every person in that group gives it a flat refusal.
The passage does not say Paul’s questions received silence.
Saying the world called the message foolish generalizes beyond the groups Paul identifies. He also says Christ is God’s wisdom to those who are called.
The explanation is a generic restatement of the quoted answer, with no distinct Papa Dorin voice.
The explanation mostly repeats the answer and ends with a generic contrast.
The passage does not say people stumble over the message because they were expecting something else.
The explanation invents a sequence in which those called previously stumbled over the message and then came to see it as power and wisdom.
The arm-wrestling joke makes God’s supposed weakness the subject of the humor.
The explanation simply repeats the quoted word and has little of Papa Dorin’s voice.
The explanation is a flat contrast followed by a repetition of the answer.
The explanation merely quotes the answer and calls it the reason on the page.
The explanation is a generic restatement of the quote, with no distinct Papa Dorin voice.
